verifications.verifierNote: Confirmed, and stronger than the discoverer knew. Pattern verified at migrate.ts:106-118: `status: legacy.status ?? 'Want to Read'` (110), `priority: legacy.priority` with no default at all (111), `rating: legacy.rating ?? 0` (112), `readingTimeMinutes: legacy.readingTimeMinutes ?? 5` (115) — all over an interface (migrate.ts:17-36) that declares current-app unions (`priority?: Priority`, `status?: BookStatus`) for values produced by `JSON.parse(raw) as T` at migrate.ts:58. `??` guards nullish only; anything else is written verbatim by repo.ts:54-59. verifications.verifierNote: Pattern confirmed, consequence confirmed, but the 'that is not hypothetical' claim is wrong and the severity has to come down with it. Verified at repo.ts:7-10: `getAll('profiles')` is typed `Profile[]` solely from the db.ts:8 DBSchema declaration, and line 9 calls `a.createdAt.localeCompare(b.createdAt)` with no guard. The consequence chain is real and I checked all of it: ProfileContext.tsx:30-42 runs `void (async () => { ... })()`, so a throw is an unhandled rejection — not caught by src/app/ErrorBoundary.tsx (that is a router errorElement, routes.tsx:16, and the throw is outside render) — and `setIsLoading(false)` at line 41 never runs, so App.tsx:12-18 renders the spinner forever with no in-app recovery. Two corrections, both measured. (1) `Array.prototype.sort` does not invoke the comparator for arrays of length < 2 — I ran it: 0 calls on a 1-element array, 1 call on a 2-element array. So the single-profile boot, which is the overwhelmingly common case, cannot throw here even with a corrupt record; you need >=2 profiles. (2) No in-app producer can write a non-string createdAt. The only writers are repo.ts:24 (`input.createdAt ?? new Date().toISOString()`) fed by migrate.ts:95, and repo.ts:31 fed by ProfileView's editor, which touches only name/bio/monthlyGoal/favoriteVoice/theme. And the legacy producer that migrate.ts:95 reads declared `joinedAt: string` and only ever wrote `new Date().toISOString()` (git show 670b5fe:App.tsx:20 and 670b5fe:components/ProfileView.tsx, which has no joinedAt setter). So the crash requires a hand-edited localStorage profile blob or a hand-edited IndexedDB record, plus a second profile. Downgraded to medium: the unvalidated read boundary and the string method on an unchecked field are genuinely worth fixing (a future writer or an older-schema record makes it live, and the failure mode is a bricked app), but it is refactor-safety, not a live bug.

verifications.verifierNote: The pattern and the mechanism are exactly as described; the reachability is not, so it comes down to medium. Verified at repo.ts:142-145: `record.bytes` is ArrayBuffer only because types.ts:78 says so, `record.type` is an unconstrained string, and `new Blob([record.bytes], { type: record.type })` runs with no check. I measured the stringification claim in node: `new Blob([{}], { type: 'application/pdf' })` yields a 15-byte blob whose text is exactly '[object Object]' carrying a legitimate application/pdf MIME — no throw. The consumer is as cited: BookDetail.tsx:195-201 `handleOpenPdf` does createObjectURL + window.open with no validation, so the user would get a broken tab and no error. And the grep holds — there is no instanceof/typeof/Array.isArray check anywhere in src/lib/storage production code. What refutes the severity is the producer side: I grepped every writer to the blobs store and there is exactly one, `blobs.put` at repo.ts:129-140, which unconditionally does `await blob.arrayBuffer()`. The only callers are useLibrary.tsx:51 and migrate.ts:137/143, all passing real Blobs; the library-import path (F048) never touches blobs. So no code path in the app can put a non-ArrayBuffer into `bytes`. The `{}` scenario CLAUDE.md documents is fake-indexeddb collapsing a stored *Blob* — which is precisely why the repo stores ArrayBuffer instead, i.e. the hazard is already mitigated by design. Downgraded to medium: a real unvalidated boundary on a CLAUDE.md-flagged conversion point, worth a cheap assertion because the compiler cannot stop a future writer from breaking it, but not a live bug.

verifications.verifierNote: Held at high, but one cited write path is wrong and must be replaced. Verified at src/types.ts:41-50: `readingTimeMinutes: number` is required while `oneSentenceTakeaway?` and `summaryId?` are optional, so the three fields that jointly mean 'this book is summarised' disagree on how absence is spelled and 6 of the 8 combinations are representable. The magic-zero claim is right: useLibrary.tsx:150-160 writes `readingTimeMinutes: 0` for every Goodreads row, and GoodreadsRow.status is BookStatus (goodreads.ts:6), so such a book can be 'Finished'. The two-line contradiction is real and I read both: BookCard.tsx:89 narrows the optional and prints 'Not summarised yet' while BookCard.tsx:95 prints '0 min read' on the same card, because a required number has no absent state to narrow — and for a migrated book (F043) the same card prints 'Not summarised yet' next to '12 min read'. What is wrong: the finding's proof that 'no write path is forced to keep them consistent' cites useLibrary.tsx:82-83, which is dead code — saveSummary's only caller is BookDetailPage.tsx:44-47 via BookDetail.tsx:186, which always operates on an existing summary whose id already equals book.summaryId, so the `book.summaryId !== summary.id` branch never runs. The live producer of the inconsistent state is migrate.ts:105-119 (sets summaryId and readingTimeMinutes, omits oneSentenceTakeaway — F043) plus the Goodreads import above; I have swapped the citation. Severity stays high despite F043 carrying the concrete bug, because this is the type-level cause in the core domain type (33 files import from src/types.ts), it has a different fix from F043, and it covers a second live inconsistency (Goodreads) that F043 does not.
